\textbf{Generalizability.} While our study examines one VLA architecture and benchmark, normalization type and gradient flow are architectural choices common to all auxiliary-head VLA fine-tuning pipelines. The BN running-statistics corruption mechanism is not architecture-specific; any model using BatchNorm in auxiliary heads with gradient flow faces the same risk. We expect the qualitative pattern (detach gradients, prefer LayerNorm) to transfer, though quantitative effect sizes may vary.

One possibility: collision avoidance demands fine-grained trajectory control near obstacles, where small perturbations cross obstacle boundaries; task success tolerates larger deviations.
